fact: Tanzania Revenue Authority's Shinyanga manager said on 27 January 2026 that the IDRAS domestic tax system is connected to AI so taxpayers can ask tax questions without visiting an office, with IDRAS due to start on 9 February 2026.

The Tanzania Revenue Authority says an AI system, adopted in November 2023 on its electronic tax stamp platform, notifies it when a stamp code is scanned in different locations, flagging duplicated codes.
The Tanzania Revenue Authority says inspections rose to 1 million scans in 2024 from 250,000 the year before and that detected fake stamps saved billions of shillings.
A Muhimbili University researcher says Tanzania already uses AI through the Ministry of Health to support TB diagnosis from chest X-ray images.
